title: Aurelia - adaptive cache cohort weekly sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on adaptive cache cohort results. Discussed drop in KV hit rate during peak, experiments with cohort-specific TTLs and prompt normalization, and next benchmarks to run (24h + tail latency). Agreed on action items: run deterministic prefix experiment, update prefetch heuristics, and share new metrics dashboard link.
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-09-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 50 minutes
Redwood: Sophie Chen (AE), Marco Patel (SE), Jordan Li (CSM)
Customer: Priya Nair (ML Eng), Liam O'Connor (Platform), Navdeep Singh (CTO), Elena Martinez (SRE)
Call type: POC weekly sync - caching
Notes: recording enabled, Fireflies auto-transcript
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, hope the time works. quick agenda — KV hit rates, prefix reuse cohort, eviction tuning, and next run benchmarks.
[00:18] Priya: yup that's good, we'll go deep on the numbers. we're seeing the hit rate fall off after 3pm UTC, which is our busiest window.
[00:32] Marco: ok, to set context, last week we deployed the adaptive-cohort TTL change that shortens TTL for high-churn keys and extends for stable prefixes. overall hit rate improved 6% but we saw a spike in tail latency.
[00:46] Liam: spike meaning what magnitude? our SLA's 200ms P95 for interactive calls, production is nudging 280 lately.
[00:58] Marco: right, P95 moved to about 310 in the window where eviction churn increased. suspect background re-population is contending CPU on the serving nodes.
[01:12] Navdeep: are we sure that's re-population and not some prefetch oscillation? we did enable prefetch heuristics two weeks ago.
[01:20] Sophie: good point. Marco — did the logs show increased prefetch thundering?
[01:26] Marco: logs indicate prefetch requests increased 2.5x for cohort B (session-based users). but because of slight tokenization differences, many prefixes don't exactly match and miss the cache — k, so we think prompt normalization would help.
[01:38] Priya: we're still sending full multi-turn context sometimes, so prefix variance large. we can add prompt normalization and stem out user-specific tokens.
[01:46] Elena: also curious about KV cache size for this cohort — could we be evicting too agressively?
[01:52] Marco: cohort B was assigned a smaller slab historically. we rebalanced but maybe not enough. table shows slab size 1.2GB vs cohort A 3.4GB.
[02:05] Sophie: remind me — cohort A are enterprise customers with more repeated prompts?
[02:10] Priya: yeah cohort A is mostly customer support flows that repeat common prompts, while B is exploration sessions.
[02:18] Marco: proposal: run two parallel experiments over the next 72 hours: (1) deterministic prefix normalization + soft TTL increase for cohort B, (2) background prefetch rate limiter to avoid re-population spikes. collect P50/P95/P99 latency and per-cohort hit rates.
[02:36] Liam: sounds good. can you also capture token-cost delta? our finance team watches that.
[02:40] Marco: will do — metrics sheet will include cost per 1M tokens.
[02:46] Sophie: action on prompt reuse — Priya, can your engs produce a small normalization library (python snippet) to run in staging?
[02:54] Priya: yes, we can. should we use aggressive normalization or conservative first?
[02:58] Marco: conservative first — strip user IDs, timestamps, but keep semantic tokens. aggressive might reduce quality.
[03:06] Priya: ok we'll push a PR by friday.
[03:10] Jordan: FYI we'll put the PR link in the pilot board.
[03:14] Sophie: Security question — storage of normalized prompts, any PII risk? Navdeep?
[03:20] Navdeep: normalized prompts remove PII by design; still need to ensure logs don't retain raw prompts beyond our retention policy. Elena, can you confirm SRE side retention?
[03:28] Elena: current retention for logs is 30 days in staging; we'll add a mask for raw prompt blobs and ensure KMS encryption.
[03:36] Liam: about dedicated vs hosted — this POC is on hosted but if we keep needing lower warm-up jitter maybe dedicated reserved nodes help. Cost tradeoff though.
[03:44] Sophie: we'll provide a cost vs latency estimate if you want to model dedicated vs burst capacity.
[03:50] Priya: yes please, that would help procurement.
[03:54] Marco: another observation: reply tokenization differences between our tokenizer and your client-side preprocessor caused prefix misalignment — calls where user included punctuation at end were treated as different prefix.
[04:06] Priya: that explains a lot. we'll sync tokenizers and add a light normalizer client-side.
[04:12] Navdeep: can Redwood's routing do session affinity so we hit the same serving pod for a session? reduces cold KV state.
[04:20] Marco: we have session affinity support in the routing layer; it's a toggle and we can enable it for subset of requests. warning: it can reduce effective autoscaling but improves KV locality.
[04:32] Liam: acceptable as a short trial.
[04:35] Sophie: ok so experiment matrix: enable session affinity for cohort B 30% traffic, enable conservative normalizer, increase slab for cohort B by 1GB, and rate-limit prefetch.
[04:48] Priya: what about eviction policy? LRU vs LFU? we saw LRU thrashes with short-lived prefixes.
[04:55] Marco: switching to a segmented LRU or windowed LFU has helped other customers. we can push a windowed-LFU parameter and simulate.
[05:04] Priya: can you simulate with our trace sample?
[05:07] Marco: yes — we'll run a 24h replay against the recent trace. need the sanitized trace.
[05:12] Priya: I'll drop a sanitized gzip in the shared drive — link: https://redwood.app/sandbox/aurelia/trace-20260920 (note: placeholder link).
[05:24] Marco: perfect. we'll run the replay and return a short report with hit-rate delta by cohort.
[05:30] Jordan: on metrics, Jordan to add P99 prefetch failures to dashboard.
[05:34] Sophie: metrics cadence — agreed daily report for next 3 days then back to weekly.
[05:40] Liam: timeline wise, pilot needs to show stable P95 under 220ms in two weeks for us to recommend expansion.
[05:48] Sophie: understood. that's the success criteria.
[05:52] Navdeep: one more thing — regression testing for output quality after normalization. we need an eval suite.
[05:58] Priya: we have 200 prompt ground-truth pairs, will run a nudge test.
[06:02] Marco: please share eval results; if quality drops more than 2% we'll rollback normalization.
[06:08] Sophie: ok, wrapping — recap of action items and next steps.
[06:12] [-- brief cross-talk as people confirm items --] 
[06:30] Sophie: thanks all, we'll send updated pilot board and schedule a short mid-week check if the 24h replays look noisy.
[06:40] Priya: thanks, see you next week.
[48:30] [meeting end]
action_items: Marco Patel: run 24h trace replay with windowed-LFU and session-affinity toggle; produce hit-rate and latency delta - due 2026-10-01
Priya Nair: sanitize and upload recent 48h request trace to shared drive (link in channel) - due 2026-09-29
Priya Nair: implement conservative prompt normalizer PR for staging and share PR link - due 2026-10-02
Elena Martinez: confirm log retention/masking changes and document KMS configuration - due 2026-10-03
Jordan Li: add P99 prefetch failure metric and cost-per-1M-token view to dashboard - due 2026-10-01
next_steps: Run two parallel experiments (deterministic prefix normalization + soft TTL; prefetch rate limiter) for 72 hours
Enable session affinity for 30% of cohort B traffic during experiments
Share cost vs latency estimate for dedicated reserved nodes vs hosted burst option
Daily metrics digest for 3 days, then weekly cadence
Follow-up sync in one week; optional mid-week ad-hoc if replays unstable
